name: list_sessions
description: List the developer's coding sessions with state (working, needs_you, done), folder, when they last wrote to it, what it is doing and a preview of what it last said. By default only the sessions they are actively working in. Use scope "all" or a query to find an older one.

query.description: Part of a session title or folder name.

name: read_session
description: Read the last few exchanges of one session: for each, what the developer asked and how the agent ended its turn (its final reply). Tool calls, scripts and the narration in between are left out. Works for any session, old ones too.

id.description: A session id from list_sessions, search_history or start_session, "this" for the session on screen, "it" for the one just discussed, or part of its title.

turns.description: How many exchanges, 1 to 10, default 3. Two or three is usually enough.

name: send_message
description: Add a message to a session, as if the developer had typed it. A busy session queues it behind what it is doing; this does not stop or change the work in progress (use interrupt_session to stop it, edit_last_message to change what it was just asked). This is also how to answer a session: when the developer says "go", "sure", "continue", "yes" or "do it", send exactly those words to the session that last asked or proposed something. Sessions found by search_history can be messaged too.

id.description: A session id from list_sessions, search_history or start_session, "this" for the session on screen, "it" for the one just discussed, or part of its title.

name: interrupt_session
description: Stop the turn a session is running, like pressing Escape.

id.description: A session id from list_sessions, search_history or start_session, "this" for the session on screen, "it" for the one just discussed, or part of its title.

name: edit_last_message
description: Use this when the developer changes their mind about what they just asked a session ("actually", "no, instead", "change that to"). Corrects the last message sent to a session: stops it if it is running, rewinds to just before that message (like /undo, including its file changes) and sends the corrected text.

id.description: A session id from list_sessions, search_history or start_session, "this" for the session on screen, "it" for the one just discussed, or part of its title.

name: start_session
description: Start a brand new session in a folder with a first task. Only when the developer asks for a new or separate session. Never use it to answer, continue or carry out what an existing session proposed ("go", "sure", "continue", "yes" go to that session with send_message), and never to retry, restart or recover a session. folder is a path, a folder name the developer has used, or "same" for the folder of the session being discussed.

name: search_history
description: Find a session anywhere in the history, including old ones that are no longer in list_sessions and what was said inside them (like Cmd+G in OpenCode). Use ordinary words from its title or conversation. Returns up to 8 sessions, best match first, with an id that read_session, send_message and close_session accept.

query.description: Words to look for, such as "library digitization pilot" or "semantic search benchmark".

name: close_session
description: Close a session: stop what it is doing and remove it from Agent View, the developer's list of sessions in focus. Its history is kept and search_history can still find it. Use when the developer says close, kill, remove, get rid of, clean up or dismiss a session.

id.description: A session id from list_sessions, search_history or start_session, "this" for the session on screen, "it" for the one just discussed, or part of its title.

name: watch_session
description: Tell the developer when a session finishes or needs them.

id.description: A session id from list_sessions, search_history or start_session, "this" for the session on screen, "it" for the one just discussed, or part of its title.

name: end_call
description: Hang up the voice call when the developer says they are done ("that's all", "bye", "hang up", "end the call"). The call stops a few seconds later, so say a short goodbye.
